Explain how a household keeps a rain barrel clean through the summer: a tight lid against mosquitoes, a screen on the inlet, rinsing it twice a year, and why the water is for the garden and not for drinking unless it is filtered and boiled first.

Walk a reader through charging phones and a radio from a car battery without running the engine in a closed garage. Name the adapters people usually own, how long a charge takes, and the one mistake that drains the battery.
Describe a week of meals that need no refrigerator: shelf-stable milk, peanut butter, crackers, canned fish and fruit. Say how to rotate them into everyday cooking so nothing expires on the shelf.
Cover what to do when the sump pump stops during a storm: check the breaker, the float switch and the outlet, move valuables upstairs, and when it's time to call someone rather than wade in.
Help a family plan who picks up the kids if the phones are down: a written card in each backpack, a meeting spot a short walk from school, and a friend out of town everyone calls to check in.

Teach the basics of keeping a cooler cold for three days: pre-chill it, pack it full, keep it in the shade, open it as little as possible, and use a thermometer so nobody guesses whether the food is still safe.
List the tools for a simple home repair kit (tape, tarps, a utility knife, zip ties, a flashlight) and explain how to cover a broken window until a glazier can come, without climbing a ladder alone.
Explain how to keep pets calm and safe in a storm: a carrier they already know, two weeks of food, a copy of their shot records, and a recent photo in case one gets out.
Describe how to stay warm in one room when the heat is out: close off the others, hang blankets over the doors, layer clothing, eat often, and never bring a grill or camp stove inside.
Walk through checking on an elderly neighbor after a power cut: knock, ask about medicines that need cooling or power, offer a phone charge, and write down who else on the street can help.
